> (auto generated by Claude)

## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4.1 dense prefill indexer (`dense_prefill_topk`) tiles the `[rows, keys]` logits of a chunk by query rows under a memory budget, and DeepGEMM strides each tile's row blocks (`128 // heads` rows) over one CTA per SM. At long context the budget gives tiles that end in a mostly empty wave, e.g. 1308-row tiles at 400K compressed keys are 2.2 waves on 148 SMs, so every tile pays for 3.

## Changes

`flat_index_logits_rows_per_tile`: on CUDA, a tile of more than one wave is rounded down to a whole number of waves (`128 // heads * num_SMs` rows). Tiles only shrink, so the logits stay within the budget; tiling is by rows, so the results are unchanged.

## Validation (B300, `dense_prefill_topk` as V4.1 calls it: 32 heads, top-k 512, DeepGEMM 0.2.3.post2 + DeepSelect)

Median of 9, cold L2, CUDA graph (eager agrees within 1-2 %). Top-k identical in every cell (up to DeepSelect's existing bf16 tie nondeterminism, also present between two runs of main).

| chunk rows x max compressed keys | tiles main -> this PR | main (ms) | this PR (ms) | ratio | peak logits MiB |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 x 64K | 2 -> 3 | 3.108 | 3.130 | 1.007 | 1033 -> 971 |
| 16384 x 128K | 4 -> 5 | 6.068 | 6.095 | 1.004 | 1029 -> 893 |
| 16384 x 200K | 7 -> 7 | 10.341 | 9.253 | 0.895 | 1027 -> 928 |
| 16384 x 262K | 8 -> 10 | 13.359 | 12.030 | 0.900 | 1027 -> 891 |
| 16384 x 400K | 13 -> 14 | 23.480 | 18.081 | 0.770 | 1025 -> 927 |
| 16384 x 500K | 16 -> 28 | 26.398 | 23.161 | 0.877 | 1026 -> 580 |
| 3392 x 500K | 4 -> 6 | 5.550 | 4.840 | 0.872 | 1025 -> 579 |
| 1533 x 262K, 507 x 131K (untiled) | 1 -> 1 | | | 1.000 | unchanged |
| real V4.1-Flash chunk, 6144 x 175K | 3 -> 3 | 3.719 | 3.262 | 0.877 | 1025 -> 992 |
| real V4.1-Flash chunk, 16128 x 139K | 5 -> 5 | 6.833 | 6.484 | 0.949 | 1027 -> 945 |
| real V4.1-Flash chunk, 16128 x 183K | 6 -> 7 | 8.453 | 8.478 | 1.003 | 1027 -> 831 |

Synthetic cells are a single request at the end of its context (causal per-row lengths, compress ratio 2) with random fp4 inputs; DeepGEMM time does not depend on the data.
